clue.text: Unlimited sums chasing professionals cycling Nice stage

indicators.note: to cycle is to go round, so a letter moves from the front of the word round to the back
to chase is to come behind, so this piece is placed after the others

parts.note: pros is the short form of professionals
the French city's name with its first letter moved to the end

indicators.note: without limits means without its boundary letters at either end, leaving only the inside

parts.note: the word with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: A cyclist racing through Nice on a stage of a professional tour, with endless sums to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice stage' reads as a leg of a cycle race; Nice is the city, and the stage is a theatre's. NICE cycled gives CENI, and UM comes last because it chases the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The proscenium is the part of a theatre in front of the curtain, so it is the front of the acting platform.

clue.text: Commend minimum wage increase for American in Britain?

indicators.note: the least possible amount of the word is just its opening letter

parts.note: a wage is pay, and the first letter of that is kept
a raise is the American word for a pay increase
surface padding: the question mark teases that Britons would say rise instead

explanation.surface: A question about whether the minimum wage increase an American would call a raise is praiseworthy over here.
explanation.walkthrough: The wage gives only its initial letter of PAY. 'In Britain?' points out that the British say pay rise where Americans say raise.
explanation.definitionFit: To commend someone is to speak approvingly of them, which is exactly what praising does.

clue.text: Disadvantaged child Oscar managed to acquire pub

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: acquiring something means taking it in, so one piece ends up inside another

parts.note: ran a business means managed it
PH, public house, is the map abbreviation for a pub

explanation.surface: A deprived youngster called Oscar has done well enough to buy a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: PH for public house is a common abbreviation on Ordnance Survey maps; it sits inside RAN, after O.
explanation.definitionFit: A child who has lost both parents is an orphan, the classic case of a child at a disadvantage.

clue.text: Film first F1 race … ooh excited!

parts.note: taken as written
the digit 1 is read as the letter I
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The 1 of F1 becomes the letter I in the fodder. The film is fitting: it is about a race too.
explanation.definitionFit: Chariots of Fire is the 1981 Oscar-winning British film about runners at the 1924 Olympics.

clue.text: Invest thousand in fresh horse back from Ascot racecourse

explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a famous English racecourse, a decoy for the one wanted; only its last letter is used. The thousand is invested between the R and E of the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket in Suffolk is the historic home of British flat racing, with two well-known courses.

clue.text: Temperature hot, leaving sign of storm beneath

T is the symbol for temperature
H for hot, as on a tap

explanation.walkthrough: T and H come off the front of THUNDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Under and beneath are synonyms as prepositions, both meaning at a lower position than something.

clue.text: Security service uncovered bones

explanation.walkthrough: Mossad is the Israeli security service; uncovered, it loses M and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossa is the Latin plural of os, used in anatomy for skeletal parts.

clue.text: Gentleman grabbing head of really large animal

explanation.definitionFit: A squirrel is a bushy-tailed rodent, a specific example of a creature or beast.

clue.text: Funny story upset Italian hothead bored by City bash

explanation.surface: A comic tale about a hot-headed Italian getting upset at a boring City party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian hothead' looks like a person; it is the volcano, a classic crossword hothead. The City is the financial district of London, whose postcodes begin with those two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short amusing account of a real incident, typically told in conversation.

clue.text: How much is that rubbish #Wed team?

taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The # symbol must be read out in full as HASHTAG to supply its letters to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: What's the damage is a colloquial way to ask for the bill, asking the price of something.

clue.text: Highest grade, record breaking Norwegian band

clue.text: Misery, US TV medical series screening rated, finally, PG

explanation.definitionFit: P. G. Wodehouse, the comic novelist who created Jeeves and Wooster, is known by those two initials.

clue.text: Endurance enlivens 13 Across when lacking energy

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is used for its word, RETIRED, as an instruction to go backwards. ANIMATES loses an E, then turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is the staying power to keep going physically or mentally over a long period.

clue.text: Refugee exhausted, weary, went to bed

indicators.note: an exhausted thing is emptied out, so its inner letters go and only the ends remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
weary means tired

explanation.surface: A worn-out refugee, tired from travel, finally goes to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhausted' and 'weary' look like a pair of synonyms; the first empties out the refugee, the second supplies TIRED.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire for the night is a formal idiom for going off to sleep.

clue.text: Playing ten snooker frames — tense time in the city …

explanation.definitionFit: Stoke-on-Trent is a Staffordshire city formed from six pottery towns, and it hosts snooker events.

clue.text: She's always up for a row!

definitions.text: She's always up for a row!

parts.words: She's always up for a row!

setter's reading: a row on the water, pulling a boat with oars

explanation.definitionFit: A female rower who propels a boat with oars is always ready for some time on the river.

clue.text: Hunt Great Bear?

parts.note: surface reading: go after a huge wild animal
setter's reading: the Great Bear is the constellation Ursa Major, sought in the night sky

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the bear is not an animal but a group of stars; hunting for it means scanning the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Searching the night sky for constellations such as Ursa Major is what an astronomer does.

clue.text: Likely weak, wanting drug when injected with arsenic and iodine

indicators.note: an injection puts something inside the body, so pieces go into the word

explanation.walkthrough: Only one of the two Es in the weak word is dropped; the two chemical symbols then go in where the first E stood.
explanation.definitionFit: Feasible can mean plausible or probable, as in a feasible explanation.

clue.text: … snooker player, one tucking into these exotic dishes from here

the Roman numeral for one

clue.text: Bird droppings endlessly fed to island area reptile
